[detail-upgrade-medicare-advantage] Scope and completeness check: started from rosters/medicare_contracts_cms_2026_09.csv (CMS MA/PDP contract directories, Sept 2026) grouped as in categories/medicare-health-insurance.json. All 44 roster parent-organization groups with >=20,000 enrollees were worked: 43 were upgraded to tier=detailed (CarePlus, Navitus MedicareRx, Freedom Health, Optimum HealthCare, VNS Health, HealthSun, MediGold, Allina Health Aetna, Astiva, KelseyCare, Imperial, Clever Care, VIVA, Prominence, ConnectiCare, Zing, Leon, UHC Community Plan OH, IEHP DualChoice, CommunityCare OK, Health First, CareSource MyCare Ohio, ATRIO, Simply, Central Health, Jefferson, Molina CA, L.A. Care, MG Insurance (MedImpact PDP), Aetna FIDE IL, Elderplan, Doctors HealthCare, Capital Health Plan, Commonwealth Care Alliance, Solis, Fallon, Saint Alphonsus, CarePartners of CT, HealthTeam Advantage, LI NET, BayCare, Blue Medicare Advantage (Elevance group retiree), Mass General Brigham); Ultimate Health Plans stays roster because no official site was reachable (CMS e-mail domain ulthp.com does not resolve; ultimatehealthplans.com is a parked page) - its CMS phone/address were added. PACE: the 5 largest PACE parents by Sept 2026 enrollment were detailed - InnovAge/Total Community Options (11 center entries; service_area corrected from CO to each center's state), WelbeHealth, AltaMed, Providence (OR, WA, Napa CA) and Trinity Health PACE (12 program entries); CenterLight (#6) remains roster. Cost/HCPP plans: all 7 privately billed cost plans in the file were detailed (Medical Associates Health Plan IA/IL and WI, DeanCare Gold, NY Hotel Trades Council fund, Union Health Service, C&O Employees' Hospital Association, CARE railroad plan); the other cost contracts (Medica, BCBS MN Aware, HealthPartners, UMWA) were already inside detailed entries. Backfill: autopay_cancel and statements_history were added to 18 existing detailed entries only where a fetched page actually said how to stop autopay or where payment/claims/EOB history lives (Aetna PayerExpress, BCBSKS, BCBSM, Arkansas Blue, IBX, Select Health, Sanford, Blue Cross of Idaho, Louisiana Blue, BCBS WY, Tufts, Colonial Penn, CalSTRS, BCBS SC, PacificSource, SCAN, UPMC, Providence). For the original 108 detailed entries autopay_cancel rose from 46 (43%) to 52 (48%) and statements_history from 39 (36%) to 51 (47%). The remaining gaps are mostly carriers whose billing help is login-only or JS-rendered (Florida Blue, Healthfirst, Devoted, Alignment, Clover, Horizon, BCBS RI/AL/MN/MS, Premera, Medigap carriers) or government payers with no autopay (SSA, RRB, OPM, TRICARE). Key findings: most of the upgraded plans are $0-premium or dual-eligible (D-SNP/FIDE/MMP) plans with no premium bill - those entries say so and leave pay/autopay links null rather than inventing them; where a premium or Part D late-enrollment penalty can exist, the EOC/enrollment-form payment options (mailed bill, plan EFT, card, SSA/RRB withholding), due dates and non-payment rules were recorded. ConnectiCare and Central Health Medicare Plan (both Molina) post notices that their Medicare coverage ends Dec 31, 2026. Method/limits: pages were fetched with curl (HTTP/1.1 - several plan sites fail over HTTP/2), PDFs parsed with pdftotext, and JS-only or bot-blocked sites (Prominence, hf.org, carepartnersct.com, mahealthplans.com, Navitus, Astiva, Zing, Fallon, MGB, BayCare, Humana LI NET page) were rendered in the browser pane; web search was unavailable this session (budget exhausted), so discovery relied on official sitemaps, site navigation and CMS directory e-mail domains. verified=true means the cited pages were fetched or rendered this session and matched; MG Insurance and Blue Medicare Advantage are verified=false (no plan-specific page). Not captured: VIVA Medicare premium-payment options (EOC PDFs truncated by the server), Jefferson/VNS EOC payment sections (JS document viewers), C&O Method of Payment form (scanned image). REVIEWER PASS (DU-REVIEW 2026-09-30): I checked this change set again on 2026-09-30. Completeness: I re-ran the CMS Sept 2026 roster check. All 44 parent groups with 20k or more enrollees, the 5 largest PACE parents and all 11 cost/HCPP contracts now sit inside detailed entries. Ultimate Health Plans (H2962, 22k) was upgraded to detailed: http://ulthp.com redirects to the official site www.chooseultimate.com, and its 2026 EOC gives the Part D penalty payment options and the Orlando lockbox PO Box 919791. CenterLight PACE (#6) is still roster. Accuracy: I re-fetched all 301 distinct URLs in the change set with curl (HTTP/1.1) and keyword-checked each link against its field. 285 returned HTTP 200. The rest were bot blocks or temporary errors: freedomhealth.com and youroptimumhealthcare.com showed 'Down for Maintenance' (HTTP 503); mahealthplans.com returned 403 to curl; Elderplan hit a local DNS failure but loaded fine once the resolved IP was pinned. One link was dead: the BCBSM low-income-subsidy URL returned 404. Fixes: (a) I cleared autopay_cancel on Aetna Medicare, Aetna FIDE, Allina Health Aetna and UHC Community Plan, because those pages only explain setting up autopay, never stopping it. An Allina note that said otherwise was corrected. (b) BCBSM: the mail addresses were wrong. PPO/PDP use P.O. Box 88512 and Medigap uses P.O. Box 88513, both Chicago IL 60680; BCN uses P.O. Box 33608, Detroit 48232. I also added autopay_cancel (Medigap autopay authorization PDF), the EOB help page, the Reduce Mail paperless page, and replaced the 404 Extra Help link. (c) Trinity Health PACE (12 entries): view_bill/pay_bill pointed to an eligibility page, so I set them to null. I added program phone numbers from the program contact pages listed in the trinityhealthpace.org sitemap. Mercy LIFE's service_area now includes MA (contract H0809). (d) Providence PACE: I removed view_bill links to program pages that have no billing content and added the WA phone. (e) Added verified member-services phones for Providence Medicare Advantage, UPMC for Life, BayCare and Allina. (f) Updated BayCare Plus to baycare.org (301 redirect) and BCBS WY to yourwyoblue.com (redirect). (g) Added Dean's own low-income premium-subsidy page. (h) Where no plan-specific page exists, payment_assistance now points to an official Medicare.gov page (fetched): Extra Help for MA/PDP plans, Medicare Savings Programs for dual/FIDE plans and CalSTRS, the PACE page for PACE. Each such entry says so in its notes. Change-set link coverage after review (97 detailed): view_bill 49, pay_bill 57, autopay_setup 35, autopay_cancel 17, statements_history 61, paperless 7, payment_assistance 92. For the original 108 detailed entries in medicare-health-insurance.json: autopay_cancel 52 (48%), statements_history 51 (47%). Remaining gaps: most upgraded plans are $0-premium or dual plans, so no bill or autopay pages exist. Login-only billing (Florida Blue, Humana, Devoted and others) still lacks a public autopay-cancel page. Web search was unavailable (budget exhausted), so discovery used sitemaps. REVIEWER PASS 3 (2026-10-01): Completeness: I re-checked against rosters/medicare_contracts_cms_2026_09.csv and the raw CMS contract directory. All 44 parent groups with 20k or more enrollees are detailed, plus the top-5 PACE parents and the 7 privately billed cost plans. Duplicate removed: 'Commonwealth Care Alliance Massachusetts' (H2225, 19,006 enrollees) is the same legal entity as the detailed 'Commonwealth Care Alliance, Inc.' (H1486). It has the same CMS phone and website, so it was merged into that entry (H1486 + H2225, about 45k enrollees). Upgraded the next-largest MA roster groups that could be reached: GlobalHealth (OK, 19.5k), Banner Medicare Advantage (AZ, 18.3k) and Johns Hopkins Advantage MD (MD/VA, 15k). From fetched pages I captured: premium and late-enrollment-penalty payment options, lockbox addresses, member-services phones, claims/EOB portal, Extra Help and the nonpayment rules. Banner's member portal and online payments moved to bpnmemberportal.bannerhealth.com in Aug/Sep 2026. bannermedicareadvantage.com now redirects to an unrelated broker site and is not used. Not upgraded: CalOptima OneCare (site returned HTTP 429), Health New England and CenterLight PACE (TLS certificate errors from this environment). Accuracy: I re-fetched all 321 distinct URLs in the change set with curl. The local network gave intermittent connect failures, so failures were retried one at a time. After retries every link resolved except: login-only portals (401/406, expected); mahealthplans.com (403 bot block, as before); and a few hosts that stayed unreachable from this environment (carehealthplan.com root/PDF, healthsun.com root, selecthealth.org, bcbsm.com pay page, allinahealthaetnamedicare.com root, unionhealth.org, portal.myultimatehp.com). Those links were fetched in earlier passes and kept. I keyword-checked the page content of every link field in 60 entries (the change-set upgrades plus the backfilled cancel/history links). Fixes: (a) Astiva: the EOC moved from astivahealth.com/pdf/ (now 404) to Azure blob storage linked from the Plan Benefits page, so links were updated. (b) Freedom Health: the enrollment-form link now shows a 'Documents Coming Soon' placeholder, so pay_bill/autopay_setup were cleared and the payment facts kept in notes. (c) SCAN: payment_processor corrected to U.S. Bank eBill, as the eBill page says. (d) ConnectiCare: the autopay_cancel note now says the Premium Payment Form is a change-method form with no cancel wording. Verified that BCBSKS, Sanford, CalSTRS, CARE, IBX, Tufts and Colonial Penn cancel links contain explicit stop/cancel/termination language. Change-set link coverage after this pass (100 entries, all detailed): view_bill 50, pay_bill 59, autopay_setup 37, autopay_cancel 17, statements_history 63, paperless 8, payment_assistance 95. medicare-health-insurance.json now has 501 entries: 190 detailed, 311 roster. [state-health-assistance-premiums] REVIEWER PASS 2026-10-02: 144 entries (121 detailed, 23 roster, 134 verified). Re-checked all 227 distinct URLs with curl. Every one returned HTTP 200 except bot-blocked hosts: mass.gov, hhs.texas.gov, kancare.ks.gov, omig.ny.gov, dhhs.nh.gov, eohhs.ri.gov, humanservices.arkansas.gov and sco.ca.gov return 403 or a challenge to scripts. The mn.gov pages sit behind a Radware CAPTCHA, which was not bypassed. Re-read about 30 detailed entries and filled their links, phones and mailing addresses. New premium pay paths: IL HBWD (Illinois E-Pay/Collector Solutions); CO Buy-In (PEAK online, mail, drop-off, plus PEAK FAQ for autopay setup/stop and history); MN MA-EPD (DHS Web Payments via U.S. Bank E-Payment, recurring payments and a stop link; upgraded to detailed and verified); NE MIWD (statement and check rules); NC HCWD (DHHS Controller address from notice DHB-5146); NJ WorkAbility (DMAHS premiums PO Box per N.J.A.C. 10:72-9.6 and 2026 premium tiers); UT MWI and spenddown (pay DWS); MS WD examples; MD EID hardship exemption. VA MEDICAID WORKS is premium-free, NY MBI-WPD premiums are under moratorium, and MN client-option spenddown auto-withdrawal has been retired. Estate recovery: IL (lockbox, correspondence box, hardship application), OR (EAU phone, toll-free, fax, email, PO Box), NE (general and case lines), WI (handbook and PO Box), AL (hardship form) and CT (DAS Recovery 860-713-5400 and PO Box 601, Manchester, now confirmed on an official page; upgraded to detailed). Arkansas was upgraded from an unverified roster entry to a detailed, verified entry using the official Medical Services Policy Manual (20 CAR pt. 500, sections H-600/H-730: TPL Unit Decedents' Estates address and hardship rules). Delaware now cites DSSM 20500 and the DMMA Customer Relations line but is still unverified because there is no official unit page. Buy-in roster entries NV HIWA, SD MAWD and VT MWPD are now verified against official pages; none publishes a premium. Property-tax deferral: payoff/repayment rules added for ID, ME, MN, WA, IL and Cook County. Added Montana Medically Needy cash-option pay-in (detailed) and Utah county property-tax deferral (roster). Earlier-pass scope still applies. SPAPs were checked against the NCSL list; only NY EPIC (fee) and VT VPharm (premium) bill recurringly and WI SeniorCare charges a $30 annual fee. Estate recovery covers all 50 states plus DC. Buy-in covers 43 states; AL, DC, FL, GA, HI, OK, SC and TN appear to have none. Most estate recovery units still have no online pay page; payment is by check to the address on the claim letter. || PRIOR PASS NOTES (counts superseded by the line above): Pass 2 (2026-09-30, continued): estate-recovery, buy-in, spend-down and property-tax gaps from pass 1 were researched with web search plus direct fetches of official pages (curl/WebFetch; JS- or bot-protected pages read in a browser; CAPTCHA pages were not bypassed). SPAPs: checked against NCSL 'State Pharmaceutical Assistance Programs'; all senior-relevant state programs listed there are included (HIV ADAPs, kidney programs and discount cards excluded). NV Senior Rx/Disability Rx ended 12/31/2023 and CT ConnPACE no longer exists, so they are omitted. MA Prescription Advantage stops taking new applications after 9/11/2026. Only NY EPIC (quarterly fee bill) and VT VPharm (monthly premium) send a recurring bill; WI SeniorCare has a $30 annual fee; the others are subsidies or copay programs (noted per entry). Estate recovery: all 50 states + DC have an entry. 49 are now verified with an official unit page, brochure, manual or regulation. In pass 2, AZ, CO, DC, FL, HI, ID, KS, KY, LA, MD, MO, MT, NM, NY (OMIG), NC, OK, VT, VA and WV were upgraded to detailed (phone/mail/hardship), and NJ, WY, NV and MN got contact details. CT (DAS Collection Services), RI (regulation 210-RICR-10-00-4) and AK (DPA manual 507) have verified official pages but no unit phone. AR and DE are still unverified roster entries pointing at the agency home page. Most states take payment by check to the address on the claim notice. Only OH (Attorney General portal) publishes an online pay page. Several states use HMS/Gainwell as the vendor (CO, FL, NM, NC, NY, WV, KS, AZ). Medicaid buy-in: 43 state entries. States with no entry (AL, DC, FL, GA, HI, OK, SC, TN) have no buy-in program as far as we found. Payment pages and processors where published: GovHub (MassHealth), Fiserv BillerDirect (IN, RI, LA billerpayments), lq-pay (MI), AccessGov (OR EPD participant fee), WA, WI ACCESS, PA MAWD online, MO portal; lockboxes for WY EID and WV M-WIN (HMS-collected, check/money order only). The following programs have no current premium and are flagged as such: CA 250% WDP ($0 since 7/2022), DE MWD (discontinued 7/2024), NY MBI-WPD (moratorium) and NM WDI (no premiums). WY EID and ND end at age 65. AK and NH (MOAD) explicitly cover working people 65+. SD, NV HIWA and VT MWPD are still unverified roster entries. MN MA-EPD is CAPTCHA-blocked. Spend-down/share of cost: MO, NY, UT, IA, WA, IL (pay-in spenddown) and FL (Medically Needy share of cost) are detailed, and CA SOC/Part B is verified. MN is CAPTCHA-blocked. The national patient-pay explainer is unverified. Other medically-needy states (NJ, PA, NC, KS, etc.) pay providers directly rather than the state and are not individually listed. Property-tax deferral: OR, CO, WA, MN, ME, ID, IL (+Cook County), MA 41A, TX (Comptroller info sheet + Form 50-126; repay to county tax collector) and FL (s.197.252; county tax collector) are detailed. CA PTP is detailed but unverified: it has SCO phone/email from San Mateo County's official page, but sco.ca.gov is behind a Cloudflare bot check. WI WHEDA deferral loan was added (very small program). DC and local-option states (NH, GA, MD, VA, MI, CT) remain roster entries. County-level administrators (TX appraisal districts/tax offices, FL tax collectors, VA localities) and Utah/Hawaii county deferrals are not enumerated.

entries.notes: No website confirmed (CMS directory lists only a compliance/contact e-mail). CMS directory contact phone (plan administrative contact, not necessarily member services): 1-251-287-8420. Members should use the number on their plan ID card. DETAIL-UPGRADE 2026-09-30: Trinity Health PACE (Trinity Health Corporation, about 3,100 participants in 12 programs). Eligibility Requirements page (fetched): services are typically free to seniors who qualify for Medicare and Medicaid or Medicaid only; participants who do not qualify for Medicaid are charged a monthly fee and may pay privately; enrollment is not restricted by Medicare/Medicaid status. Each program has its own page and contact-us page on trinityhealthpace.org (state/program paths, e.g. /alabama/mercy-life-of-alabama/contact-us). No online payment, autopay or mailing address is published - call the PACE center. DU-REVIEW 2026-09-30: view_bill/pay_bill cleared: they pointed to the Eligibility Requirements page, which explains who pays (Medicaid-eligible participants usually pay nothing; others pay a monthly fee or pay privately) but not how to view or pay a bill. That page stays as payment_assistance. The Trinity Health PACE FAQ (fetched) says payment depends on Medicare/Medicaid eligibility and over-income/asset participants pay monthly fees. Program contact page (fetched; listed in the trinityhealthpace.org locations sitemap) gives the phone numbers now recorded. Call the center about private-pay fees. LINK-BACKFILL 2026-09-30: Member-cost page, used because no plan premium is billed to most participants. The program's eligibility page (fetched 2026-09-30) says services are 'typically free to seniors who qualify for Medicare and Medicaid or Medicaid only'. Participants who do not qualify for Medicaid are charged a monthly fee and may pay privately. There is no copay or deductible, and the monthly private-pay amount is set by the program. That page is used as pay_bill. No online payment, autopay, statement or paperless page is published; private-pay participants arrange billing with the program office (see phone).

entries.notes: No website confirmed (CMS directory lists only a compliance/contact e-mail). CMS directory contact phone (plan administrative contact, not necessarily member services): 1-800-633-1542. Members should use the number on their plan ID card. REVIEW 2026-09-29: website filled from a homepage fetched this session (title 'Home | Viva Health'). DETAIL-UPGRADE 2026-09-30: Member Resources page (fetched) 'Monthly Premium' section: 2026 plan premiums are $0 for Plus, Select, Extra Value, Classic, Extra Care and Infirmary Health Advantage, and $99/month for Viva Medicare Premier (LIS members on Premier pay $71.30); members keep paying Part B to Medicare. The page lists the 2026 EOC for each plan (e.g. https://www.vivahealth.com/files/general/2026-premier-eoc), which contains the premium-payment options, but the server truncated the PDF downloads this session so the options could not be read; pay_bill/autopay links stay null - call Member Services. Member Services correspondence: Viva Medicare, 417 20th Street North, Suite 1100, Birmingham, AL 35203 (not confirmed as a payment address). Member login vivamembers.com (claims/EOB). The page notes members can review their monthly Part D Explanation of Benefits. Owned by Triton Health Systems (UAB affiliate). LINK-BACKFILL 2026-09-30: The My Membership page (fetched) lists 2026/2027 monthly premiums: only Viva Medicare Premier (HMO) has a plan premium ($99); Plus, Select, Extra Value, Classic, Extra Care, Infirmary Health Advantage and Healthy Lifestyles are $0, so no plan premium is billed for them (members still pay Part B to Medicare). The 2026 Premier EOC (fetched, Chapter 1 Section 5.1) lists four ways to pay: check against a monthly billing statement mailed to you (due the 1st; $20 NSF fee; no walk-in payments), EFT from a bank account (EFT Authorization Agreement from Member Services plus a voided check), Social Security deduction, or Railroad Retirement Board deduction. To change or stop a payment method call Member Services 1-800-633-1542 (TTY 711); a change can take up to 3 months. Members get a late notice if the premium is not received by the 5th, and membership ends after 60 days unpaid. The same EOC is used for view_bill, autopay_setup and autopay_cancel.

entries.name: Montana Medicaid Medically Needy spend down - Cash Option (pay the spend down to DPHHS)
entries.parent_company: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide; medically needy Medicaid (aged, blind, disabled and family)
entries.senior_programs: Medicaid spend-down / excess income: seniors whose income is over the Medicaid limit can qualify each month by incurring medical bills or, in some states, paying the excess amount to the state ('pay-in').
entries.notes: Combined Medicaid Manual CMA 701-1 "Cash Option" (effective 1/1/2022, fetched 2026-10-02). Medically needy clients may meet their monthly spend down by paying the exact spend-down amount in cash to the Department. Once the payment is processed, Medicaid is issued for the full month. The amount can be reduced by allowable expenses: paid or unpaid medical bills from the 3 prior months, health insurance and Medicare premiums, and non-covered medical expenses. The cash option is not available to people receiving VA Aid & Attendance. It can be used for retroactive months. The manual gives no payment address; the spend-down notice from the local Office of Public Assistance gives remittance instructions. The manual PDF is reused as view_bill and pay_bill.

Only people who are billed directly (not having premiums deducted from Social Security/RRB/OPM benefits) get the quarterly or monthly 'Medicare Premium Bill' (CMS-500). Covers Part B premium, premium Part A (for people without 40 work quarters), Part B late-enrollment penalty.

entries.notes: Four ways to pay: (1) online in Medicare account > My premiums (fastest), (2) Medicare Easy Pay automatic deduction on the 20th of each month (bank statement shows 'CMS Medicare Premiums'; sign up/stop online via My premiums or by mailing form SF-5510; start takes 6-8 weeks, stop up to 4 weeks), (3) bank online bill pay to payee 'CMS Medicare Insurance' with the 11-character Medicare Number, (4) mail. Payment history: Medicare account > My premiums > Payment history. Most people have Part B deducted from Social Security, RRB or OPM annuity and never receive a bill. Official page says credit card by mail via coupon; there is no pay-by-phone option listed. [Link backfill 2026-09-30] Medicare Easy Pay page (fetched 2026-10-02) answers 'How do I change bank accounts or stop Medicare Easy Pay?' (Medicare account > My Premiums > See or change my Medicare Easy Pay, or mail SF-5510); stopping can take up to 4 weeks. Easy Pay enrollees get a monthly 'Medicare Easy Pay Premium Statement' (CMS-20143) instead of a bill. No paperless option for the CMS-500 premium bill was found on medicare.gov (its sitemap has no paperless premium-bill page) and no pay-by-phone line exists - pay online, Easy Pay, bank bill pay or mail.

entries.name: Social Security Administration - Medicare premium deductions & IRMAA (Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount)
entries.service_area_detail: Nationwide. SSA deducts Part B premium, Part B IRMAA and Part D IRMAA from Social Security benefits; people not receiving benefits get IRMAA billed by CMS on the Medicare Premium Bill (CMS-500). Part D IRMAA is paid to Medicare, not to the drug plan. Also where MA/PDP plan premiums are withheld (premium withhold option).
entries.payment_processor: Social Security benefit withholding; otherwise CMS bill
entries.senior_programs: Request lower IRMAA after a life-changing event (marriage, divorce, death of spouse, work stoppage/loss of income, employer settlement) with Form SSA-44: sign in and submit online, or fax/mail to a local office. Call 1-800-772-1213 for amended tax returns. Apply for Part D Extra Help online at ssa.gov/medicare/part-d-extra-help.
entries.notes: www.ssa.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches this session, so the ssa.gov URLs (lower-irmaa, SSA-44 form) are unverified; the POMS IRMAA sliding-scale table (secure.ssa.gov) was fetched (HTTP 200). IRMAA amounts for 2026 are also published by RRB (rrb.gov news release). For the app: an IRMAA notice is not a separate bill if premiums are withheld from benefits; if not, IRMAA appears on the CMS Medicare Premium Bill and is paid via Medicare (see Original Medicare entry). REVIEW-2 2026-09-30: ssa.gov still returns 403 to curl/WebFetch, but these pages were read in a real browser this session. The Lower IRMAA page links the SSA-44 PDF and the online SSA-44 upload flow. The Extra Help page has an online application. The Manage Medicare benefits page says people whose premiums are not withheld from Social Security are billed by CMS, and lists the ways to pay Medicare (online account, Easy Pay, bank bill pay, mail to the Medicare Premium Collection Center). It is recorded as pay_bill because it sends people to the CMS bill; see the Original Medicare entry. SSA itself has no pay-by-phone or autopay service for premiums. [Link backfill 2026-09-30] SSA itself has no autopay enrollment page: Social Security withholding of Part B, IRMAA and (on request through the plan) Medicare Advantage/Part D premiums happens automatically from monthly benefits. To start or stop withholding of a private plan premium, the member contacts the plan (see each carrier's 'ssa_rrb_premium_deduction' link); withholding changes typically take 1-3 months. Medicare Supplement premiums cannot be withheld by SSA.
